title: Lecture 15 — memory arrays and stored outputs
summary: Decode addresses into stored words, connect ROM to combinational logic, and compare SRAM, DRAM, flash and multiport memories.
body:
An address selects a word; it is not the word itself. Begin with depth, width and total capacity, keeping bits and bytes separate. A decoder selects one row, while the stored connections or cells determine the output bits. This makes a ROM a physical truth table.

The counter-decoder-memory-display chain connects Lecture 12 to memory: the counter chooses the position, the decoder selects that row, and the stored word specifies what to display. Track active-low signals and any output inversion before deciding what a diode connection means. Practise with invented words before applying the method to your own work.

Then compare the storage mechanisms. SRAM maintains a powered feedback state; DRAM stores charge and needs refresh and read restoration; ROM and flash retain data without power but have different programming constraints. Finally distinguish capacity from ports: additional read ports permit more simultaneous accesses without multiplying the stored words. Canvas places this lecture before Lectures 13 and 14 to prepare for Lab 4.
